cap: Benign glands, normal or hyperplastic, keep two cell layers: a basal layer under the secretory layer, which p63 stains. Adenocarcinoma forms small, crowded glands with a single secretory layer, little stroma between them, prominent nucleoli and perineural invasion, so p63 is negative and AMACR is positive. The cancer cell is a luminal secretory cell and often carries a TMPRSS2-ERG fusion.
teach: The diagnosis rests on architecture and the missing basal layer, not on size: BPH can make a very large gland, while a small focus of cancer can be silent. High-grade PIN, with atypical cells inside glands that still have a basal layer, is the likely precursor. Gleason grading scores the glandular pattern, from well-formed glands (3) through fused and cribriform glands (4) to sheets of cells without glands (5); the two commonest patterns are added into a score and grouped into Grade Groups 1 to 5.
